nodes.statement: The framework applies only when the authoring process is version-controlled with attribution.
nodes.span: The artifact has a commit or revision history with attribution.
nodes.status_reason: Stated as a boundary condition without derivation.

nodes.statement: The framework applies only when the artifact contains propositional claims with truth conditions.
nodes.span: The artifact contains identifiable propositional claim markers with truth conditions.
nodes.status_reason: Stated as a boundary condition without derivation.

nodes.statement: The framework applies only when there is a non-trivial divergence between the author's and the audience's schemas.
nodes.span: Measured lexical or structural distance between the author domain and the target cohort domain exceeds a threshold.
nodes.status_reason: Stated as a boundary condition without derivation.

nodes.statement: The framework applies only when the volume of artifacts is too large for unaided human verification.
nodes.span: The artifact volume per unit time relative to the community's reviewer capacity is large enough
nodes.status_reason: Stated as a boundary condition without derivation.

nodes.statement: Knowledge artifacts can be decomposed into a log of authoring events, a structured graph of claims (spine), and a cohort-specific prose rendering.
nodes.span: decomposes a knowledge artifact into three layers — a log substrate (L) of authoring events, a semantic substrate or spine (S)
nodes.status_reason: Introduced as a foundational definition of the framework.

nodes.statement: The Operator role consists of structural substrate operations, which are era-dependent, and judgment operations, which remain with humans.
nodes.span: The role's intrinsic operations split into two classes with qualitatively different projection patterns.
nodes.status_reason: Introduced as a foundational definition of the framework.

nodes.statement: AI verification of the structured spine scales sub-linearly, whereas human verification of the prose rendering scales super-linearly.
nodes.span: Generative AI bifurcates the cost of knowledge work asymmetrically across the substrate / rendering boundary
nodes.status_reason: Asserted as an observable structural condition of generative AI.

nodes.statement: The extraction of the spine from the log and the generation of the rendering from the spine are independent processes.
nodes.span: Meaning and meaningfulness are separately optimizable: $\sigma : L \to S$ without consulting any R
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the definitions of the three-layer decomposition.

nodes.statement: A faithful rendering allows the extraction operator to recover the locked elements of the spine.
nodes.span: when a rendering preserves the locked elements of the spine, the $\sigma$ extraction operator recovers them.
nodes.status_reason: Stated as an explicit axiom.

nodes.statement: Two different prose renderings of the same locked spine will yield the same conclusions if and only if both preserve the spine's structural elements.
nodes.span: two prose renderings of the same spine arrive at the same set of conclusions iff both renderings preserve the spine's structural elements.
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the three-layer decomposition and the faithfulness axiom A1.

nodes.statement: Organizations that publish the structural spine of their artifacts achieve higher rates of knowledge recombination than those that only publish prose renderings.
nodes.span: Organizations that publish the substrate of their knowledge artifacts as a first-class artifact achieve higher rates of knowledge recombination
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the cost asymmetry and the queryability of the published spine.

nodes.statement: Allocating AI to verify the spine and humans to make sense of the rendering results in lower total verification costs.
nodes.span: organizations that allocate AI projection to substrate verification and reserve human projection for rendering sensemaking realize lower total verification cost
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the cost asymmetry and the Operator role partition.

nodes.statement: The Eisenhardt & Martin and Zollo & Winter papers on dynamic capabilities share the same underlying structural propositions despite using different formalisms.
nodes.span: their structural isomorphism across the two papers' formalism boundary is the framework's P4 prediction instantiated
nodes.status_reason: Empirical observation from a historical management-theory twin pair.

nodes.statement: Independent authors in the Kulkarni et al. paper arrived at the same underlying substrate propositions through different prose renderings.
nodes.span: The multiple-discovery pattern within a single multi-author paper is itself an instance of the framework's central claim
nodes.status_reason: Empirical observation from a contemporary multi-author paper.

nodes.statement: The historical equivalence of matrix mechanics and wave mechanics demonstrates that different formalisms can converge on the same conclusions.
nodes.span: Schrödinger himself then proved that matrix mechanics and wave mechanics are mathematically equivalent in the equivalence paper
nodes.status_reason: Historical observation from the founding papers of quantum mechanics.

nodes.statement: The framework is reflexively applied to this paper itself, demonstrating that the spine-first protocol can produce a coherent set of renderings.
nodes.span: exhibits the framework reflexively by publishing its own substrate as a Zenodo companion artifact and tracing every prose claim
nodes.status_reason: Observation from the reflexive self-application of the framework.

nodes.statement: Organizations should treat the structural substrate as a governed asset and publish it alongside prose renderings.
nodes.span: Organizations operating under C1–C4 should publish the substrate of their knowledge artifacts as a first-class governed asset alongside renderings.
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the recombination advantage proposition P2.

nodes.statement: Roles and incentives should be redesigned to separate structural-substrate operations from judgment operations.
nodes.span: redesign Operator roles around the structural-substrate / judgment partition rather than around the legacy task-level workflow.
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the verification-cost asymmetry proposition P3.

nodes.statement: Academic peer review should evaluate the structural coherence of the substrate separately from the prose craft of the rendering.
nodes.span: evaluate substrate coherence and prose craft as separate inputs rather than as a single rolled-up review verdict.
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the separability proposition P1 and verification-cost asymmetry P3.

nodes.statement: Generative AI hallucinates citations when given only prose renderings without access to the underlying claim graph.
nodes.span: An AI operating on R alone reconstructs a plausible-sounding S from rendering-shaped tokens because S is not exposed
nodes.status_reason: Empirical observation of AI behavior.

nodes.statement: Replication failures often occur due to differences in how the same underlying claims are rendered into measurement protocols.
nodes.span: replications often fail not because the underlying claim is wrong but because the rendering of the claim into a measurement protocol differs
nodes.status_reason: Empirical observation from replication initiatives.

nodes.statement: Cross-language translations preserve the underlying claims but lose the cohort-specific register and narrative cues.
nodes.span: the underlying claims translate cleanly while register, citation-density expectations, and narrative-arc cues do not.
nodes.status_reason: Empirical observation from bilingual reading practices.

nodes.statement: Scholarly artifacts maintain the same conclusions across different rendering mediums like prose, podcasts, and slide decks.
nodes.span: Properly specified scholarly artifacts exhibit conclusion-invariance across rendering medium — prose, podcast, slide deck, infographic, video
nodes.status_reason: Empirical observation from scientific communication practices.

nodes.statement: The spine-first drafting protocol requires locking the structural substrate before drafting prose and tracing every prose claim to a substrate entry.
nodes.span: locking the substrate before drafting prose; tracing every prose claim to a substrate entry; surfacing orphan claims
nodes.status_reason: Follows logically from the cost asymmetry proposition.

nodes.statement: The spine-first protocol is prospectively applied to a publicly available organizational methodology handbook to demonstrate its utility on non-self artifacts.
nodes.span: we apply it prospectively to a publicly available organizational methodology handbook.
nodes.status_reason: Prospective application proposed as evidence.
